{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABcZR2dw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhF8CUI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 97, "title": "Redesign Play UI into a simple disc-first Saturn web player", "body": "## Problem

The browser Play page is still presented as a showcase for the bundled homebrew games: the document title and hero promote **Star Collector**, the player toolbar exposes "Play Star Collector" and "Play Prism Courier", explanatory sections advertise those samples, and the default boot selection is the HLE bootstrap debugger fixture rather than a normal disc-loading flow. Users who simply want to load their own Saturn disc must find the nested "Load disc / BIOS & boot settings" disclosure, distinguish boot modes, and then navigate back to Play. This makes the product look like a demo gallery rather than a straightforward Saturn web player.

Redesign the **user-facing Play experience** using the **second UI concept from the design discussion**: a clean, dark, **two-column layout with a large 4:3 player on the left and a right-hand four-step disc setup flow**. Keep the visual treatment restrained: deep navy/charcoal, subtle blue highlights, crisp typography, clear hierarchy, and no commercial-game screenshots or mock gameplay presented as real emulator output.

The reference concept is a layout and UX target, **not a claim that every illustrated control already exists**. Avoid unnecessary features, fake playback states, and misleading format/BIOS assurances.

## Expected outcome

Opening the site shows a neutral **Saturn Disc Player** (or similarly simple product title), **not a preselected/demo game**. The left column has a prominent, responsive 4:3 screen; before media is loaded it shows a quiet empty state such as "Load a disc to begin" with a subtle disc/ring motif, not fake game footage. Beneath it are playback controls and a collapsed advanced/debug area.

The right column visibly guides first-time users:

1. **Select disc** — primary, accessible file selection and drag-and-drop area with privacy reassurance; show the chosen file(s) or actionable validation errors.
2. **Add BIOS (if needed)** — an optional local 512 KiB BIOS picker, plus a clear explanation of when HLE versus user-supplied firmware is selected. No automatic BIOS download, and no suggestion that retail BIOS/game compatibility is guaranteed.
3. **Choose boot mode** — expose only **real implemented modes** (BIOS-less HLE disc vs. user-provided BIOS; optionally move the HLE bootstrap debugger fixture into advanced/debug). Do **not** implement the concept image's "game/CD data" choices or a claimed reliable "automatic" BIOS detection unless supported and validated separately.
4. **Start playing** — one clearly identifiable primary Start/Play action, disabled until the selected mode has its required input. Once running, show only useful play/pause, restart/reset, audio enable/status, fullscreen and relevant progress/error messages; do not duplicate competing Start controls.

The visual hierarchy should make loading **your own disc** the product's purpose, without changing or falsely expanding emulation compatibility.

## Context and reproduction

Checked `main` at `628b0b85dacc6b53722687ebcc82b13261c8ebd5` (2026-11-04).

- `web/index.html`: `<title>saturn-rust · Star Collector</title>`, `play-intro`, `play-homebrew` and `play-prism` sample buttons, hidden `details#settings` boot controls, and a visible Debug tab.
- `web/app.js`: the sample button handlers `fetch("./star-collector.iso")` / `fetch("./prism-courier.iso")`; current `disc`, `hle`, `bios` modes; local CUE/BIN, ISO, and now CHD input; asynchronous media/BIOS generation cancellation, reset, audio and focus behavior.
- `web/style.css` or existing web styles, `web/audio.js`, `web/audio-worklet.js`, `scripts/browser-smoke.mjs` and existing browser scenarios must be inspected/updated accordingly.
- [Issue #95](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/issues/95) was completed by [PR #96](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/96): current picker supports self-contained CHD v5 alongside ISO and CUE with BIN tracks. Reflect **actual** supported formats, restrictions and validation; do not regress that change.
- Current native Rust/Wasm/browser demo discs `homebrew/star-collector`, `homebrew/prism-courier`, and `homebrew/hardware-lab` are useful test fixtures. Removing **promotional UI and default sample launches** is not permission to delete licensed source, disc builders, tests, or CI coverage.

**Reproduction (current):** visit the browser page with no disc selected. It advertises Star Collector, defaults to an HLE debugger prototype, requires opening a secondary settings panel to find disc selection, and has two competing sample launch actions. Target: immediately see a disc-first, four-step setup beside a clean idle player.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Two-column Play composition:** implement a responsive page with a slim neutral header; large left player/display area retaining native aspect ratio (4:3 for standard modes, correct dynamic dimensions when the core changes mode); right setup column with four visually distinct ordered steps; a compact control bar beneath the display. On smaller screens, stack sections sensibly (prefer disc selection before the idle display), preserve touch-sized controls, keyboard navigation and readable text. No horizontal overflow at representative desktop/tablet/mobile widths.
- [ ] **Honest empty state:** without user media, do not auto-run or load a bundled demo; show an uncluttered idle player prompt, clear availability/status and one main path to loading a disc. Do not show invented game images, game title art, successful loading, active audio or a BIOS selected when none exists. Use subtle decorative graphics only.
- [ ] **Remove sample-centric product UI:** replace Star Collector page title, intro/marketing prose, sample download promotions, sample-specific status/recovery text, and `play-homebrew` / `play-prism` controls/handlers from the normal Play workflow with neutral disc-player copy. Keep existing original game/diagnostic fixtures, build outputs and automated coverage intact; do not remove files solely because they are no longer promoted. Update help/README copy to match.
- [ ] **Disc step and drag/drop:** visibly accept the current supported CHD v5 CD-ROM, cooked ISO, and CUE + all referenced BINARY track files (and the pre-existing explicitly optional SRW1 companion when applicable). Handle multi-file selection and drop safely; **a lone raw BIN is not automatically a valid disc**. Clearly show file names, size/selection, replacement and missing-track errors. Use the existing media APIs and limits rather than extracting files, uploading data, requiring another tool/sidecar, or silently changing formats.
- [ ] **BIOS and boot clarity:** retain separate real HLE-disc and user-BIOS execution modes, with a 512 KiB local BIOS picker shown as optional for HLE and required for user-BIOS mode; make the selected mode explicit and explain known limitations without promising commercial-game support. Do not silently fall back from BIOS to HLE. Preserve the existing developer HLE bootstrap fixture under advanced/Debug, not as the user-facing default.
- [ ] **Single straightforward launch flow:** Step 4's primary Start button is actionable only when the current mode and required selected files are valid and fully read/loaded; loading and failure states are visible and non-misleading. Avoid premature success, accidental duplicate starts, stale asynchronous file loads, forced auto-resume on settings/view changes, or losing media/backup bytes unexpectedly. Preserve safe replacement, reset/restart, pause/resume and focus-release semantics.
- [ ] **Player controls and advanced functionality:** retain actual frame rendering, playable keyboard/gamepad inputs, audio user-gesture enable and meaningful blocked/mute/underflow indications, pause/resume, Restart/Reset and fullscreen with graceful failure handling. Keep Debug (CPU state, Step, bounded Run, frame advance, reset) and backup RAM import/export available in clearly separated advanced sections, without crowding the first-time loading flow. Show concise status/errors rather than large noisy debug logs in the player.
- [ ] **Visual/UX quality:** use accessible labels and status announcements, visible focus outlines, coherent disabled/loading states, good text contrast, and predictable navigation. Favor functional minimalism over device-shaped chrome, large decorative marketing, status badges everywhere, or decorative controls that do nothing. Keep existing copy language consistent; the Japanese labels in the concept are content examples rather than a mandate for an unrelated localization project.
- [ ] **Privacy/security:** all selected disc/BIOS/save data remain local, with no automatic upload, analytics, CDN, network retrieval of user media or implicit persistence. Respect existing CSP, file picker and memory-lifetime rules; preserve clear privacy/backup export messaging.
- [ ] **Automated validation:** update and preserve native/Wasm/Chromium scenarios for old sample-fixture execution via explicit test mechanisms, and add realistic Play UI tests for initial empty screen, selecting local ISO/CUE+BIN/CHD, BIOS mode, dropped multi-file CUE, bad/missing input, asynchronous replacement/cancellation, start/stop/restart, view/focus/visibility events, audio gesture and basic responsive layout. No proprietary game/BIOS required. Run applicable build/format/Clippy, fixtures, browser tests and CI (see `docs/development-flow.md` and `docs/ci-performance.md`); report actual results and any newly required runtime assets.
- [ ] **Documentation:** describe the normal user flow (select disc → optional BIOS → choose actual boot mode → start), supported image formats and limitations, existing privacy model, basic controls, and where advanced debugger/backup features moved. Do not imply that a redesigned UI means retail-game compatibility.

## Optional validation

Screenshots/layout comparison to the second UI concept at common viewports; a small independent usability pass; accessible reduced-motion styling. Do not make manual approval, a personal BIOS, real commercial game images, physical console, or live Pages browsing a blocking criterion.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Native/Wasm/browser tests and layout assertions must be executed before merge; live Pages publication is not a required acceptance gate.
